answer: Cryptographic sortition selects each agent proportionally to its stake via a VRF proof unforgeable and unpredictable. Tickets are non-transferable, so a selected node cannot delegate its status. An attacker scanning the horizon for exploits gains nothing by splitting stake across Sybil clones, as total selection odds stay identical. Each inlet into a consensus round is independently drawn, so cloning merely redistributes fixed odds rather than multiplying them. The attacker must still buy visible on-chain stake in the open ocean of the ledger, making saturation prohibitively expensive.
